title: Adaptive license envelopes and emergency-patch SLAs for private VPCs
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic packaging option for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that separates baseline license economics from time-sensitive operational guarantees. Many enterprise prospects ask for: (a) predictable license caps for committed capacity, (b) clearly scoped upgrade/patch cadences, and (c) a paid emergency-patch SLA for high-risk regulated customers. This ticket defines an experiment to introduce 'adaptive license envelopes' combined with an opt-in Emergency Patch SLA (EPSLA).

Goals:
- Create simple license bands (Small/Medium/Large/Committed) expressed as vGPU-months and seat-equivalents.
- Offer a non-intrusive EPSLA as an add-on: 4-hour emergency patch window for critical security fixes with concierge coordination.
- Define upgrade cadences (Regular: quarterly; Accelerated: monthly; Controlled: customer-approved windows) and map to pricing offsets.
- Produce contract and security questionnaire language that reduces legal friction for security teams.
- Measure win-rate uplift, time-to-sign, and incremental revenue from EPSLA.

Proposed packaging (experiment):
- Baseline License (included): Annual license fee by band with 1. Standard quarterly upgrade cadence; 2. Standard support (business hours) and security questionnaire responses within 7 business days.
- Adaptive Envelope: Customers can purchase +/-20% burst headroom in monthly vGPU consumption billed at a blended overage rate; envelope resets monthly.
- EPSLA (paid add-on): 4-hour response target for emergency patches during business hours, dedicated runbook + remote assist, guaranteed staging within 12 hours. Priced as a percentage uplift on annual fee (suggested 10-25% by band) or flat per-instance premium.
- Upgrade windows: 'Regular' (no additional fee, quarterly), 'Accelerated' (monthly, +5% fee), 'Controlled' (customer-scheduled, includes compatibility testing, +10-15% fee).

Success metrics (90 days after GA):
- 10% increase in closure rate for Enterprise Proof-of-Concepts citing upgrade SLAs as blocker.
- 20% attach rate for EPSLA among customers classified as regulated (HIPAA, FINRA, etc.).
- No more than two legal negotiation escalations per quarter on patch language.

Open trade-offs and questions:
- Pricing model: percentage uplift vs flat fee per instance. Flat fee is simpler for sales but may under-index value for larger installs.
- Operational load: EPSLA requires runbook automation and on-call rotations for Private deployments; we must decide if engineering will support patch execution or only validation.
- Billing: support for monthly envelope resets and overage calculations in billing platform (requires ENG changes).

Required engineering scope (high level):
- Billing changes to support envelope tracking and overage calculations (ENG-1842).
- Upgrade orchestration tooling for 'Controlled' windows; ability to stage and rollback in private networks (dependent on ENG-3891).
- Telemetry hooks for measuring patch timing and SLA compliance.

Contracts and compliance artifacts:
- Draft contract clauses for EPSLA and Adaptive Envelope (attached to this ticket as Drive links).
- Security questionnaire templates with pre-approved language for EPSLA (Confluence: /PrivateDeployments/Security/EPSLA-template).
- Example SOW for 'Controlled' upgrade engagements.

Experiment plan and timeline:
- Week 1-2: Legal and Security alignment on EPSLA clauses and questionnaire language. Owners: Legal (Leah Myers), Security (Tomás Rivera).
- Week 3-5: Build sales materials and pricing calculator; pilot with 3 active opportunities. Owner: Solutions (Maya Li).
- Week 6-10: Engineering changes for billing and telemetry in a limited beta. Owner: ENG (see ENG-1842).
- Week 11-12: Evaluate pilot results, iterate on pricing bands or EPSLA pricing, prepare for GA.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRD/pages/564321/EPSLA+and+Adaptive+Envelope+PRD
- Draft contract language (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcXAMPLEepsla
- Pricing calculator (Sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XyzEXAMPLEpricing
- GitHub engineering stub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8432

Notes on legal/security feedback so far:
- Security flagged the need for verifiable proof-of-patch in private networks; suggested inclusion of a 'patch receipt' artifact signed by customer admin.
- Legal requested clearer definitions of 'critical security fix' and exclusions for third-party stack components.

Next steps:
- (This week) Kickoff legal review meeting and lock EPSLA contract language. Owner: Ravi Patel.
- (Next week) Sales to identify three pilot customers and capture baseline objections. Owner: Maya Li.
- (2 weeks) Finalize pricing bands and publish internal sell-sheet. Owner: Product Marketing (Jonah Price).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering scope creeping if EPSLA requires hands-on patching across multiple customer environments. Mitigation: Limit scope at launch to remote verification and guided customer execution; revisit hands-on patching after telemetry and automation are mature.
- Risk: Customers demand shorter-than-offered patch windows. Mitigation: Document escalation path and offer custom SOWs for <4 hour windows at premium pricing.
